info.title: Pulso API
info.description:
Pulso is a conversational CX measurement platform. The integrator triggers a conversation by posting to a single endpoint and Pulso reaches the customer through the chosen channel: phone (outbound Twilio call), email (transactional invitation with a signed link to the web chat), or whatsapp (approved `pulso_es` template). The AI agent runs the conversation, the analysis pipeline scores it, and the configured action tools fire when the action plan triggers them.

## Authentication

Every request requires an API key issued from the Pulso console, sent as a Bearer token:

```
Authorization: Bearer pk_live_...
```

The key is scoped per tenant. The endpoint documented here needs `conversations:write`.

## Base URL

Production: `https://api.pulso.cx`

Errors follow the shape `{ statusCode, code, message, timestamp, path }` and use the standard HTTP status codes (`401 UNAUTHORIZED` when the bearer token is missing or invalid, `403 FORBIDDEN` when the key lacks the scope, `422 VALIDATION_ERROR` when the payload fails schema validation).

tags.name: Conversations
tags.description: Start an AI-driven conversation on any supported channel.

post.description:
Creates a new conversation row, resolves the customer identity, and triggers the appropriate outbound action based on the requested `channel`:

- `phone`: places an outbound Twilio call to `channelMetadata.phoneE164`. The agent speaks in real time over the call.
- `email`: sends a transactional invitation via SES to `channelMetadata.email`. The mail contains a signed link to `chat.pulso.cx/p/{shareSlug}?ct=...` (TTL 7 days) so the customer answers on the web chat without re-identifying themselves.
- `whatsapp`: sends the approved `pulso_es` template via Meta Cloud API to `channelMetadata.phoneE164`. The customer answers in WhatsApp and the agent replies in the same thread.
- `web`: not exposed via the public API. Web conversations start when the customer opens `chat.pulso.cx/p/{shareSlug}` directly.

The response returns the `conversationId` immediately; the outbound side effect (call, email, template) runs asynchronously through the event bus, so the same idempotency rules apply: a retry with the same payload creates a fresh conversation, it does not deduplicate.

email.summary: Email invitation with a signed link to the web chat

201.description: Conversation created and outbound action scheduled.

403.description: The API key is missing the `conversations:write` scope.

BearerAuth.description: API key issued from the Pulso console. Send as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`.

Channel.description: Outbound channel. `web` is reserved for direct shareSlug links and is not exposed via the public API.

ChannelMetadata.description: Channel-specific payload. `phoneE164` is required for `phone` and `whatsapp`; `email` is required for `email`.

phoneE164.description: Destination phone in E.164 format (leading `+`, country code, no spaces). Required for `phone` and `whatsapp`.

email.description: Destination email address. Required for `email`. The platform upserts a client row keyed by `(tenantId, emailHash)` before scheduling the invitation, so subsequent conversations with the same address reuse the same identity.

pulsoVersionId.description: Id of the published `pulsoVersion` to run. Look it up in the Pulso console (`/pulsos/{id}` shows the live version id).

clientId.description: Optional pre-resolved client id. When omitted, Pulso resolves identity from `channelMetadata` (upsert by email for `email`; deterministic phone hash lookup for `whatsapp`).

conversationId.description: Id of the freshly created conversation. Use it to correlate the outbound side effect (Twilio call SID, SES MessageId, Meta wamid) with the analysis and action plan downstream.

startedAt.description: Server-side timestamp when the conversation row was persisted.

statusCode.description: HTTP status code mirrored in the body.

message.description: Human-readable explanation. Do not parse; use `code` for control flow.

path.description: Request path that produced the error.
